title: the WSG land-based vehicles - Table 14 (the vehicle movement rates and loads)
audit_comment: The land-based vehicles slice pins Table 14 (the 21 cart, chariot and wagon rows x the normal and rugged rates and the maximum loads), the miles-per-half-day scale, the no-very-rugged rule and the pathless one-category-worse rule (rules/wsgvehicle.h, prefix wvv); census 358 -> 359.

banner.title: The WSG LAND-BASED VEHICLES, R434: Table 14 (the movement of vehicles - the 21 cart, chariot and wagon rows by the animal team x the normal and rugged terrain rates and the maximum load in gp; a 0 in the rugged column means the vehicle cannot go there) with the prose rules: the rates are miles per half-day, no vehicle can be taken into very rugged terrain (progress effectively negligible), the rates assume flat featureless ground or a path or roadway, and without such a path the terrain counts as one category more rugged for the vehicle (the lightly-forested example) - the round continues the encumbrance-and-movement chapter. Census 358 -> 359.
banner.provenance: the WSG scan (archive.org item pdfy-B3Fz83tZ3TV7zOc8), printed p. 33; the user own copy OCR cross-checked against the archive djvu word layer (17 of 21 rows clean) and the IIIF full-resolution eye-reads (the chariot small/medium horse and the wagon rows garbled in the djvu; the eye-read values matched the user copy exactly); every number matched. The compiled-tables copy reads the cart medium/pony rugged cell as 6 - a djvu OCR error; the body text and the user copy both read 0.
banner.sentinel: The Table 14 movement figures are miles per half-day over normal and rugged terrain; a 0 rugged entry means the vehicle cannot be taken onto rugged terrain. The maximum load is the gp encumbrance value the vehicle and team can haul.

consts.name: wvvCartRowBase
consts.comment: The cart rows begin at index 0 (small and medium carts, 8 rows).

consts.name: wvvChariotRowBase
consts.comment: The chariot rows begin at index 8 (small and large chariots, 6 rows).

consts.name: wvvWagonRowBase
consts.comment: The wagon rows begin at index 14 (small and large wagons, 7 rows).

bools.name: wvvRateMilesPerHalfDay
bools.comment: The Table 14 rates are expressed in miles per half-day.

bools.name: wvvNoVeryRugged
bools.comment: None of the vehicles can be taken into very rugged terrain - or, if they are, progress is so slow as to make large-scale movement effectively negligible.

bools.name: wvvAssumesFlatOrPath
bools.comment: The given rates assume flat, featureless ground or a path or roadway.

bools.name: wvvPathlessOneCategoryWorse
bools.comment: Without a path smooth and wide enough for the vehicle, treat the terrain as one category more rugged than it actually is.

bools.name: wvvLightForestVehicleRugged
bools.comment: The lightly-forested example: normal terrain for a character on foot or mounted, but rugged for a vehicle without a suitable path.

bools.name: wvvCartsWagonsHaulGear
bools.comment: Carts and wagons transport equipment (and possibly characters) over long distances.

bools.name: wvvChariotsMainlyCharacters
bools.comment: Chariots are used mainly to transport characters; the larger ones can also haul equipment.

bools.name: wvvMaxLoadIsGp
bools.comment: The maximum load column is the gp encumbrance value the vehicle and team can haul.

tables.name: Table 14: the movement of vehicles
col_comments: The normal-terrain rate in miles per half-day by vehicle row (the carts, the chariots and the wagons by their animal teams).
The rugged-terrain rate in miles per half-day (0 = cannot be taken onto rugged terrain).
The maximum load in gp of encumbrance value.
tables.audit_comment: the Table 14 grid: the 21 vehicle rows (the small and medium carts, the small and large chariots, the small and large wagons, each by its animal team) x the normal and rugged rates and the maximum loads

examples.note: the small cart drawn by a pony: 8 and 4 miles per half-day, a 3500 gp maximum load
the medium cart drawn by a pony cannot be taken onto rugged terrain (0)
the large chariot drawn by heavy horses: the fastest vehicle, 16 and 10 miles per half-day, a 5500 gp load
the large wagon drawn by light horses: 10 and 6, a 12000 gp load
the large wagon drawn by heavy horses hauls the most: 15000 gp
